_comment: REGISTERED per-unit statement+branch coverage targets + NAMED exemptions for
Wave-2.6 (docs/twin_validation/wave2_6_unit_test_contract.md, the per-unit contract;
parent docs/twin_validation/api_hardening_ownership_design.md rows A1/A2/A3 + the
TWO-SIDED PER-UNIT EXTENSION). Audited by
outputs/twin_validation/wave2_6_coverage_audit.py (runner:
outputs/twin_validation/wave2_6_coverage_audit_run.sh).
ANTI-STALE RE-ARCHITECTURE (findings 1/3/5). This registry NO LONGER hand-writes
per-unit source line ranges. Hand-written ranges go STALE the instant a source file
is edited (the _assert_density extraction shifted fixtures.py line numbers; a registry
pinning old lines then scores the WRONG lines and can PASS while a unit's real body is
never examined). Instead each in-scope unit is identified by (module, qualname), and the
audit DERIVES the unit's statement+branch line set from the source AST at run time
(FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef by qualname, body lineno..end_lineno minus nested defs),
then intersects with coverage.py's per-file executed/missing sets. A source edit that
moves a unit's body moves its scored lines WITH it -- a stale range can no longer cause
a false PASS, and a renamed/deleted unit fails the qualname lookup loudly.
SEMANTICS (the gate the audit enforces):
* The 'units' list MUST enumerate ALL 19 in-scope units (contract SS8: A1 7 +
A2 3 + A3 3 + infra 6). An in-scope unit MISSING from this registry is a HARD
AUDIT ERROR (SS11 AM-3: closes the under-population game). An enumerated unit whose
name is not in the canonical 19-unit set is ALSO a hard error.
* Each unit pins its source by 'module' + 'qualname' (the dotted class/function path).
The audit finds that def in the source AST and scores ONLY its body's statement +
branch lines (minus nested defs) -- it NEVER counts out-of-scope lines (batched
core / GPU sample() path / trajectory body) against a unit's target (SS10 dec 5).
* A unit whose statement OR branch coverage is < its target (default 100%/100%)
AFTER removing its NAMED exemptions is an audit FAILURE (exit 1).
* Exemptions are DATA here, never inline '# pragma: no cover' in src. Each carries a
'kind', a STABLE 'selector' (AST-resolved, NOT a hard line number), a 'reason', and
a NON-EMPTY 'covered_by' list naming the test(s) that DO cover the exempted line.
An exemption is added ONLY by a reviewed diff to this file, never by
auto-regeneration. The audit re-validates every selector against the CURRENT AST
(a degraded selector -- e.g. a torch-None guard that no longer raises -- fails
LOUDLY, never a silent no-op) and verifies every covered_by test EXISTS in the
suite (a dangling covered_by is a HARD AUDIT ERROR).
EXEMPTION KINDS + SELECTORS:
torch_missing / selector {type: 'raise_in_torch_none_guard'}
-- the 'if torch is None: raise' guard; unreachable with torch
installed (the target box always has it). The audit locates the
raise inside the torch-None guard in the unit's AST body and
exempts that line. Reached only by a fixtures.torch=None
monkeypatch meta-test (SS10 decision 6), named in covered_by;
kept exempt as a structural torch-less-box fallback.
defensive_assert / selector {type: 'raise_in_callee', callee: '_assert_*'}
-- an assert-never-fires guard whose raise-side branch is
structurally unreachable for any legitimate input (SS11 BL-2,
SS12.1 DEFENSIVE-ASSERT RULE). Selected by the extracted seam's
NAME (AST), not a line number. After the BL-2 extraction the seam
is a SEPARATE function OUT of the unit's AST body, so no line is
removed from the unit's denominator -- the selector re-validates
that the seam exists, raises, and the unit calls it. Covered by
the PAIR (sabotaged-input trip meta-test + legitimate-path
property test), both named in covered_by. (No in-scope unit needs
this kind after the extraction; retained as a documented, audited
option for future inline defensive asserts.)
line (fallback) / selector {type: 'line', line: N, stmt_kind: 'raise'|'branch'}
-- allowed ONLY if a fully AST-driven selector is too complex. The
audit re-validates that line N is (a) inside the unit's CURRENT
AST body and (b) an actual raise/branch statement, failing loudly
otherwise. Not used by any current unit.
FINDING-4 DISPOSITION (leak_slice_table / _leak_sample GPU-reachable lines).
Option (a) chosen: the coverage RUN (wave2_6_coverage_audit_run.sh) already includes
the Wave-2 integration gates (test_frontend_experiments.py + test_shotset_records.py)
ALONGSIDE the wave2.6 unit test files, and this repo's gate runs are ON THE GPU BOX.
So leak_slice_table's GPU builder arms (SvSampler.build_within_cycle_leak + the
as_list return-shape branch) are genuinely EXECUTED and counted on-box (verified: in
the regenerated .coverage those lines are executed), covered by
test_leak_slice_table_matches_sv_sampler. Likewise _leak_sample's application body
(mps.gate_ / _renormalize) executes as statements under the CPU stub unit test
(no-op sinks) AND its physics is covered by the GPU AM-5 gate
test_am5_leak_sample_tiebreak_registry. Neither unit therefore carries a GPU-only
exemption -- the audit is HONEST on-box (no exemption papering over a real gap).

units.note: Module-level frozen ExperimentPreset instances (PRESET_LEAK_THETA_0P30 / PRESET_LEAK_WG_L1_5E3). This is a REGRESSION VALUE PIN, not a scored source body: construction is covered by import and every knob is pinned by exact-== field assertions in the named tests (contract SS3.4). No AST body to score; covered_by names the value-pin tests.

FINDING-4 option (a): no GPU-only exemption. The SvSampler.build_within_cycle_leak arms + the as_list return-shape branch are reachable only after the requires_cuda builder call, but the coverage RUN includes the requires_cuda integration gate test_leak_slice_table_matches_sv_sampler (tests/test_frontend_experiments.py) and this repo's gate runs are ON the GPU box, so those lines are genuinely executed and counted on-box (verified executed in the regenerated .coverage). The CPU TypeError branch (neither-preset-nor-RunSpec) is covered by a CPU unit test. If this gate is ever run on a CPU-only box, those GPU lines will show as a legitimate gap -- correct honesty, not a false PASS.

The two private helpers _require_shots (shots-None ValueError leg) and _header_geometry (missing-key KeyError leg) are SEPARATE units (SS4 'exercised through them'); they are NOT folded into to_det_obs's AST body. Their raise legs are driven through to_det_obs / packed_bytes / syndrome_prefix_bytes by the unit tests; they are not separately registered (SS8 keeps the canonical 19 count), and their coverage is subsumed by the accessor units that call them.

FINDING-4 option (a): no GPU-only exemption. The selection loop + fallback (K-3 tie-break) is exercised CPU-only via an injected pk stub (SS10 decision 3). The application body (mps.gate_ apply + self._renormalize) executes as STATEMENTS under the CPU stub unit test (the stub's gate_/multiply_ are no-op sinks the test asserts are called), and the trajectory PHYSICS is covered by the requires_cuda AM-5 gate test_am5_leak_sample_tiebreak_registry (tests/test_shotset_records.py). So the whole AST body is honestly covered on-box.

exemptions.reason: The 'if torch is None: raise RuntimeError' guard on the backend='torch' path is unreachable with torch installed (the standing target box always has it). The audit locates this raise inside the torch-None guard in random_cptp_kraus's AST body and exempts it; it is reached only by a fixtures.torch=None monkeypatch meta-test (SS10 decision 6), kept as a structural torch-less-box fallback. NOTE: the _assert_cptp defensive-assert raise is NOT in this unit's AST body (it is the separate _assert_cptp seam, out of scope after the BL-2-style extraction), so no defensive_assert exemption is needed here.

The 'if torch is None: raise RuntimeError' guard on the backend='torch' path is unreachable with torch installed. Reached only by a fixtures.torch=None monkeypatch meta-test (SS10 decision 6). NOTE: after the BL-2 extraction the internal trace/hermiticity defensive asserts live in the SEPARATE _assert_density(rho, tol) seam (module-private, out of this unit's AST body), so random_density_matrix's own body has NO structurally-unreachable defensive-assert lines -- only the torch-None guard needs exemption. The defensive-assert seam is covered by test_random_density_matrix_internal_assert_trips_on_sabotaged_rho (teeth) + test_random_density_matrix_property_hermitian_psd_unit_trace (legitimate path never fires).
